title: BCCI meeting decoded: Devajit Saikia reveals big plans for injuries, SENA tours and 2027 World Cup
description: The BCCI is set to enhance its overseas performance strategy while tackling player injuries. They aim to craft a robust plan in preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will require adjustments in the Future Tours Programme to prioritise player rest. Recent defeats in white-ball matches against England and Ireland were carefully analysed, and insight was gathered from captains and the head coach regarding fitness protocols.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has drawn up a roadmap to address India's recent overseas setbacks, mounting player injuries and preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with secretary Devajit Saikia revealing details of Thursday's high-level review meeting in Mumbai.

The meeting, attended by head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer and Centre of Excellence director VVS Laxman, reviewed India's recent tours of Ireland and England as well as the team's preparations for the next phase of the international calendar.

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar was absent, but Saikia said there was no controversy behind his non-participation and insisted no discussion took place about his future.

Saikia strongly rejected suggestions of a communication gap between the team management and the Centre of Excellence, particularly after several high-profile injury setbacks.

"Everybody is on the same page. BCCI is working in a very well like a well oiled engine," Saikia told reporters.

"There is proper coordination amongst all the wings of BCCI, whether it is women's teams committees or their technical staff or their coaches, vis-a-vis the COE, vis-a-vis the Indian men's team's coaching staff and the head coach. There is no difficulty in the coordination, everything is moving in the right direction."

However, he admitted that the frequency of injuries remains a major concern and said the board intends to address it through changes to the next Future Tours Programme (FTP).

"The only challenge which we are facing is that there are too many matches in the year and that is why in the next FTP we will do certain things, we will take certain measures."

The proposed changes will particularly affect preparation for tours to SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

"We have instructed our FTP persons who will be meeting very soon in various international forums that our FTP should be in such a way it should be scheduled that there is proper rest for the players as well as some kind of acclimatisation or some kind of friendly matches before any major series in SENA countries," Saikia said.

The comments come after India suffered a difficult run in overseas white-ball cricket, losing 0-2 to Ireland in the T20Is before a 1-4 defeat to England in the five-match series. India also lost the ODI series in England 1-2.

Saikia acknowledged India's shortcomings and said the review meeting focused on understanding why the team had struggled.

"We discussed (about) our team performed in England and Ireland and also about what we are going to do about the next one year. The road map has been prepared and we will be doing some exercises so that we have a very good performance in 2027 (ODI) World Cup," he said.

"Yes, we did not do well. We lost matches in Ireland and England, so we wanted to know what the reasons were. We have to do certain soul searching about that, and in future, what we will be doing before going to any of the SENA countries, we have chalked out some strategy on that."

The board also revisited its Return to Play protocols, with feedback sought directly from Gill, Iyer and Gambhir.

"Today's discussion was totally general in nature, what policy and protocols we have to maintain regarding maintaining the fitness level of every player -- not any individual -- and what is best interest of the team, we have considered that only," Saikia said.

"We have taken the feedback from the captains and the head coach who are the right persons to give us the information, so that we chalk up a proper strategy to avoid all this kind of unwanted situations during matches."

Saikia also pushed back against renewed speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma's ODI future and his prospects of playing at the 2027 World Cup.

"He is playing superbly in all the matches. So, what more do you want? In the last match, he scored 138 runs. So, why there is a speculation? So, I don't want to give fodder to the speculations," Saikia said.

Rohit had scored a century at Lord's in his last ODI appearance, intensifying the debate over whether he would continue until the 2027 World Cup.

Saikia also explained why Agarkar was absent from the meeting.

"Today he (Agarkar) was out of station, so he could not be a part of the meeting. Because this meeting was called at very short notice and our head of the selection committee, Ajit Agarkar, was not in town, he could not join it, and he was in such an area that he could not join online also, despite our best efforts," he said.

"There was no such discussion on this in today's meeting. I do not comment on new rumours. We did not have any such discussions, nor did we have such intentions."

He further ruled out any discussion about appointing a new director of cricket.

"There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was on performances in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka and what we are going to do in the upcoming series before the ODI World Cup, which is our ultimate goal," Saikia said.

The vacant Head of Sports Science and Medicine position at the CoE was another issue addressed by Saikia, who insisted it had not affected the centre's functioning.

"I would like to reiterate once more that the vacant position of the head of the sports science is not a deterrent of our activities in COE," he said.

"(Filling) that post is required, but that is a very high level post, and for that, a proper qualified person should be positioned. We have about 16 persons in place to maintain the fitness level or the rehab facilities."

"To supervise that one important person is required, and for that he must be qualified up to a different level. That kind of person is very less in number in India, as well as in the whole world.

"We are trying to find out that kind of a person at the earliest possible time but without him also it is running in the right manner," Saikia added.

The meeting, therefore, ended without any major immediate personnel changes, but with the BCCI setting out a broader plan: reduce the burden of an overcrowded calendar, improve overseas preparation, strengthen injury management and build towards the 2027 World Cup.

description: St Helens centre and former England international Mark Percival is to retire from rugby league at the end of the season.
fullText:
St Helens centre and former England international Mark Percival will retire from rugby league at the end of the season.

The 32-year-old has spent his entire career with Saints and during that time won five Super League titles, four League Leaders' Shields, the Challenge Cup and the World Club Challenge.

He has made a total of 273 appearances for the club since making his debut in 2013 and has missed much of this season through injury - but he has been named in Saints' matchday squad, external to face Leigh Leopards this weekend.

"This has not been an easy decision, and there's a lot of emotion around it," Percival told the club website., external

"I love this club so much, and I want to play. I want to be out there helping the team and to be with the fans, so not being able to do that has been difficult, and it makes this decision even harder.

"This is not a choice I've made overnight. It's always difficult when you have to step away, and knowing if it's the right decision can be hard too. Ultimately, I feel like this is going to be the right decision, even though my mind is telling me to play on; sadly, my body is telling me different.

"I'll be getting my shoulder replaced at the end of the year. It is what it is. Long-term it means I'll be able to pick my kids up and not deal with the symptoms I have this season, which is something I've been struggling with."

St Helens legend Lomax to retire at end of season

Catalans' Makinson to retire at end of season

Percival's retirement comes after he signed a new deal earlier this season to remain with the club until the end of the 2027 season.

He also calls time on his career at the same time as team-mate Jonny Lomax, who will also retire at the end of the current campaign.

A foot injury meant Percival missed the beginning of this season, while a hamstring injury has also limited his appearances this term to a total of seven, with his most recent coming in their win against Huddersfield Giants in June.

Percival was granted a testimonial by St Helens in 2023, the same year in which they defeated NRL premiers Penrith Panthers in Australia in the World Club Challenge.

title: Fifa accuses Uefa of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
description: The governing bodies have traded blows since Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
fullText:
Fifa has accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to litigation over president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Last week European football's governing body filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa as part of potential criminal claims in Switzerland.

In a dramatic escalation of the controversy, Uefa accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" and "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by [him] for his own benefit" over the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

However, world governing body Fifa has now responded with court filings lodged in the US - and seen by the BBC - requesting that permission for access to documents be deferred, or opposed by the end of the month.

Fifa claims Uefa's argument "suffers from a fundamental defect" and "legal deficiencies".

"Uefa seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that Uefa admittedly lacks the authority to initiate. Despite that threshold problem, Uefa asks this court to authorise sweeping discovery about the FFE."

It said it had "made clear" that the creation of FFE was "only a proposal", adding that it could have only proceeded on the condition that the majority of member associations supported it and "the relevant approvals of the Fifa Council".

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, Uefa issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership," it wrote in the court filing.

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

It also claimed that Uefa's "economic motivation" was to prevent smaller countries from having the "financial strength to compete with the European elite".

"If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces Uefa's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments," Fifa said.

"By raising funds to allow some of Fifa's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad."

Uefa has declined to comment, although BBC Sport has been told insiders believe that if Fifa has nothing to hide, it should disclose the documents and speed up the legal process. It has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down from three confederations.

Uefa has also asked a court in New York to approve a legal document ordering testimony and documents from venture capitalist Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, who was set to be the lead investor in FFE, and his company Thrive Eternal.

Thrive had held talks with Infantino about heading up a $4.2bn (£3.1bn) investment in 20% of a new Fifa commercial subsidiary, before the idea was abandoned days after it was revealed in July amid a huge backlash.

At the time, Fifa claimed FFE would have increased the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle from £5.9m to £14.7m.

On Sunday, Kushner expressed regret over FFE, saying: "While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to… had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

Uefa has also asked for the disclosure of documents from American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed".

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at about £15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". Uefa claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

title: Wong stars as England thump Ireland to seal series
description: Issy Wong's first international five-wicket haul leads England to a six-wicket win over Ireland and seals the three-match series with a game to spare.
fullText:
Second ODI, The OurCoop County Ground, Derby

Ireland 165 (47 overs): Hunter 64 (96); Wong 5-33

England 166-4 (23 overs): Bouchier 45 (31); McCartney 2-45

England won by six wickets; lead series 2-0

England sealed a comfortable series win as they hammered Ireland by six wickets in a one-sided encounter in the second one-day international at Derby.

Fast bowler Issy Wong took 5-33 - her first international five-wicket haul - as Ireland were dissmissed for 165 before England cruised to their target in 23 overs to take the series with a match to spare.

Though England made light work of the chase, they were guilty of throwing away their wickets.

Openers Maia Bouchier and Sophia Dunkley, who starred in England's record-breaking chase in the opener at Leicester, started positively with a stand of 54 in seven overs.

Bouchier, who made 45 off 31 balls, inexplicably ran Dunkley out for 20 before also carelessly being caught off a short ball from spinner Kia McCartney.

Alice Capsey was pinned lbw for one and Jodi Grewcock chipped one to mid-wicket for 24, but all-rounders Freya Kemp and Dani Gibson safely steered England to victory with an unbroken stand of 41.

Ireland's batters impressed in the opener by posting 281 but their lack of depth was exposed without contributions from the experienced duo of Gaby Lewis or Orla Prendergast here.

After Wong bowled Lewis for 19, Amy Hunter held firm with her second fifty in as many games, but struggled for support from elsewhere as she fell to Wong for 64 and Ireland lost their last six wickets for 25 runs.

The series and England's international summer concludes at Worcester on Sunday.

Though England won the opener comfortably, their bowlers were unthreatening on a flat pitch in Leicester and struggled to take consistent wickets without Lauren Bell and Sophie Ecclestone, who are resting for the series.

But Wong continued her resurgence under Charlotte Edwards' reign, and appeared to thrive with the responsibility of leading the attack as Lauren Filer was rested.

She bowled Ireland captain Lewis with a nip-backer before Prendergast wasted her solid start before holing out to deep mid-wicket for 25 off Mady Villiers.

Villiers also removed Rebecca Stokell for three, exposing Ireland's fragile middle to lower order for Wong to clean up, and they could not cope with her pace and accuracy.

Ireland managed just 10 boundaries in their innings and, to highlight the mismatch in the teams, Bouchier struck nine alone in her knock.

As the wickets tumbled, the pressure was on Hunter to steer Ireland to a competitive total, but she was caught on the boundary for Wong's fifth wicket to end a gritty 96-ball stay.

The game at Leicester was Wong's first ODI since 2024, and though the batting line-up was not of the highest quality, this was a performance that will please England and Edwards as her transition from bright, emerging talent to potential attack leader develops.

title: Chicago Fire acquire Noah Allen from Inter Miami

fullText:
Chicago Fire FC have acquired defender Noah Allen on loan from Inter Miami CF, the clubs announced Thursday.

The 22-year-old Greek youth international's loan is through the 2026 MLS season with a permanent trade option.

Allen will occupy a U22 Initiative roster slot for Chicago.

"As a young defender who has developed through the MLS ranks, Noah has consistently shown that he can compete at the highest levels of Major League Soccer," said Chicago director of football and head coach Gregg Berhalter.

"What stands out is his competitive mentality, his drive to improve and his versatile skill set. He has valuable experience for his age, and we believe he has the qualities to make an impact on this team."

Allen is Inter Miami's all-time appearances leader, featuring 132 times and contributing 3g/7a. He came through Inter Miami's academy before signing a homegrown deal in 2022.

During his time with the Herons, Allen helped the club win Leagues Cup, Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup titles. In 2025, he finished No. 12 on the league's 22 Under 22 Rankings.

"I'm thankful to have been a part of Inter Miami and its history, and to have seen the Club grow into what it is today," said Allen. "I'm just grateful that I was able to be a part of it. To everyone who helped me and for all the memories I made, I'll cherish them with me forever."

Allen continues a busy summer transfer deadline for Chicago, who have added Georgian international midfielder Anzor Mekvabishvili, Norwegian international defender Andreas Hanche-Olsen and former US youth international midfielder Johan Gómez in recent days.

Meanwhile, former Spain international Sergio Reguilón is Miami's top left back upon Allen's exit.

title: Donovan won't 'underestimate' fired-up McKenna
description: Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.
fullText:
Paddy Donovan insists he is not "underestimating" Tyrone McKenna before they meet at Croke Park on Saturday with a second crack at world honours on the horizon.

Donovan bounced back from his first title defeat by Lewis Crocker with an impressive victory over Karen Chukhadzhian in May to return to the mandatory slot for the IBF welterweight title held by Australia's Liam Paro.

The Limerick man is aware of the risks in taking a fight in the interim, but felt this was too good an opportunity to turn down and plans to put on a show to elevate his status.

He and McKenna have sparred countless rounds over the years and the 27-year-old, whose record is 15 wins with two defeats, feels he is a level above his fellow southpaw.

"It's risky to take the fight being number one with the IBF but I couldn't turn down the opportunity to fight in front of 80,000 Irish fans," Donovan said at Thursday's news conference.

"We want to bring big shows back to Ireland when Katie's gone and I'm going to be the guy to do it.

"I'm not underestimating you [McKenna], I've a job to do so I'll beat you and move onto becoming a world champion, but you're first and I'll deal with you good and proper."

'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero

Veteran McKenna [25-6-1] has lost two of his last four fights after reversing a decision to retire following his own defeat by Crocker in 2023.

However, the Belfast man is not content to play the role of gatekeeper and set up camp in Philadelphia - where he spent an early part of his career - to work in 'The Dungeon' gym of Derrick 'Bozy' Ennis - father of undefeated two-division champion Jaron 'Boots'.

"To bring a west Belfast man to north Philly is a dangerous combination," said the 36-year-old.

"This is the most I've sparred in a camp, in a world-class gym surrounded by world champions and world-class fighters. The coaching has been world-class, so I've done everything for this fight.

"I think Paddy is overlooking me as all I hear is 'Liam Paro, Lewis Crocker', but you [Donovan] have to get your mind right because I'm coming for you."

Chief support on Saturday is a heavyweight contest between Dave Allen [27-9-2] and Thomas Carty [11-1].

Doncaster's Allen admits his ambitions of fighting for top honours are over following May's defeat by newly-crowned IBF heavyweight champion Filip Hrgovic.

However, he has bounced back with a pair of routine wins and feels he remains a "proper handful" at his level.

"After the Hrgovic fight, all of the feeling for boxing left me," the 34-year-old revealed.

"I'm not trying to resurrect any run for titles, I'm just here to fight but if you're not very good, I'll flatten you."

Carty once had aspirations to play Gaelic football for Dublin at Croke Park, but on Saturday he will realise something of a dream when boxing at the home of the Gaelic Athletic Association.

His sole defeat came at Madison Square Garden in March 2025 when suffering an ACL injury against Dajuan Calloway, but the 30-year-old southpaw feels he is "probably better now than what I was before" the injury.

Another Dubliner, Emmet Brennan, will make the 500-metre journey from his house to Croke Park to face fellow unbeaten super-middleweight Taylor Bevan with added incentive of double pay by Brian Peters, who represents Bevan, should he prevail.

Meanwhile, MMA convert Molly McCann continues her boxing journey against Sylwia Doligala.

McCann, who has won all four of her bouts since making the switch to professional boxing, is a relative of headliner Katie Taylor with her late grandmother a great-aunt of the Bray woman - and she recounted her own early struggles to find acceptance in the boxing world.

"I remember walking into a boxing gym and was turned away as I was a girl," said the 36-year-old Liverpudlian.

"[I] then started boxing at the Golden Gloves gym and my coach brought in a camcorder, told me to watch this girl and lo and behold, it was Katie.

"I was like 'oh my God, I want to be like that', and 20 years later here we are. It's not lost on me how many girls would kill to be in this position, so it's an honour and privilege."

title: Iraola confirms Barcola in line for Liverpool debut against Ipswich
description: Bradley Barcola could make his Liverpool debut within days of arriving, after Andoni Iraola gave a strong hint the winger will be involved against Ipswich Town.The France international completed his m...
fullText:
Bradley Barcola could make his Liverpool debut within days of arriving, after Andoni Iraola gave a strong hint the winger will be involved against Ipswich Town.

The France international completed his move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday and has since trained twice with his new teammates.

Iraola addressed the signing at his press conference on Thursday, making no attempt to hide his satisfaction. "We are very happy with Bradley," he said. "It was our priority, let's say, to sign a very, very good player in that position."

He pointed to Barcola's attitude as much as his ability. "I think he has come also with the right mentality," Iraola said. "I've liked from him that he wanted Liverpool a lot. He just wanted to come here, and I think that's a good first sign."

The head coach also referenced Barcola's recent trophy haul with PSG, calling it evidence of the standards he can bring to the squad. "Being the player that he is and the things that he has won recently, I think he has come also with the willingness to help us," he said. "I'm very happy with him. He trained well with us."

Availability for Friday's trip to Portman Road looked close to confirmed. "If everything goes well in today's training also, he will definitely be available for tomorrow, yes," Iraola said.

Whether Barcola starts is a separate question, and one Iraola took time to consider before answering. "It's a good question, it's a good question," he said. "I see him in a good place. He has trained with us in three trainings. It's true that he hasn't had minutes in pre-season, but he has been training normal with the group. Then it's a decision we have to make."

He added a note of caution given Barcola's lack of match sharpness. "I think he's in a good place, but we also have to consider that he hasn't had the minutes in the pre-season games," Iraola said.

Barcola's arrival caps a £123m deal from Paris Saint-Germain, completed on the transfer deadline day and making him one of the most expensive signings in Liverpool's history. He last featured for France in their World Cup third-place play-off, and has not played a competitive minute since.

title: WeatherNext 3: Our most advanced global weather AI model
description: WeatherNext 3, our most advanced global weather AI model, is now in Search, Gemini, Maps, Google Maps Platform, and Cloud.
fullText:
Our flagship AI weather forecasting model now includes real-time satellite data, hourly refreshes, higher resolution, precise precipitation forecasting, and clean energy variables. It’s now integrated across Search, Gemini, Maps, Google Maps Platform, and Cloud.

Every day, the weather influences billions of decisions. Some are as simple as grabbing an umbrella before heading out the door, but others are far more consequential. Wind, rain, and extreme weather events, like heatwaves and droughts, have cascading impacts across agriculture, global supply chains, clean energy production, and national economies.

In recent years, AI has revolutionized weather forecasting, using historical records to make faster and more accurate predictions than traditional methods. Yet predicting highly local and rapidly changing weather has remained a challenge. Previous models often lacked sufficient spatial resolution, and struggled to incorporate real-time weather data from sources like satellites.

Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research are introducing WeatherNext 3, the most advanced and accurate global weather model to date, according to independent live evaluations by Brightband. Our model learns directly from real-time observations, enabling it to provide timely and more localized predictions for the weather events that impact people the most. By using raw satellite data to produce a forecast every hour in high resolution, our model makes reliable forecasts accessible across Google products worldwide.

A forecast's utility often comes down to detail and how finely it resolves both time and space. WeatherNext 3 generates hourly forecasts at multiple spatial resolutions, maintaining physical consistency from broad global wind patterns all the way down to local topography.

With WeatherNext 3, we can visualize key surface variables — like temperature and moisture — at a 5-kilometer resolution, other surface variables at 10 kilometers, and atmospheric variables, like wind speed, at 25 kilometers. Overall, this provides a global weather picture roughly five times sharper than our previous model, WeatherNext 2, which produced forecasts on a 25-kilometer grid in 6-hour increments.

Figure 1: The end-to-end WeatherNext 3 system architecture. The model ingests live 1-hour geostationary satellite mosaics alongside traditional historical analysis to feed a single, flexible Functional Generative Network (FGN) mesh transformer. It outputs dense gridded fields, discrete cyclone tracks, and predicts station-level sparse coordinates natively.

Figure 2: Comparison of 2-meter temperature forecasts over the UK. WeatherNext 2 (left) at 25-kilometer (0.25°) resolution vs. WeatherNext 3 (right) at a native 5-kilometer (0.05°) resolution. WeatherNext 3 resolves the intricate local topography, preventing the pixelated, over-smoothed thermal representations seen in older models.

WeatherNext 3's biggest leap forward is what it learns from. Most AI weather models, including WeatherNext 2, are trained on data from numerical weather prediction (NWP) models. Although useful, NWP models are complex, supercomputer-driven physics simulations that carry a six-hour data lag. This lag can lead to biases for fast-changing variables like rain or surface temperature.

This is important because critical weather develops fast. When storms, fronts, or precipitation systems materialize suddenly, our rapid update cycle and higher resolution provides earlier, more detailed insights needed to help drive an effective response.

Some variables, like temperature and humidity, can fluctuate dramatically over just a few kilometers, which is particularly relevant for communities near coastlines, valleys, or mountain ranges. Traditional models struggle here because they train on representations of the atmosphere that lack detail and miss extreme local variations.

To address this, WeatherNext 3 instead trains directly on sparse weather station observation data. This allows us to make global forecasts on a 5-kilometer grid that account for regional details like topography.

This breakthrough is particularly vital for regions across Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific that have historically been underserved by high-resolution forecasting due to the immense supercomputing costs of traditional regional models. It brings localized, high-fidelity forecasting to billions of people and local businesses in these areas.

Beyond improved resolution and forecast frequency, our model introduces predictions specifically engineered for renewable energy production. The model forecasts 100-meter wind speeds (roughly at turbine-height) for precise wind-energy output, alongside high-resolution cloud cover and sun radiation levels to help solar farms estimate how much light they will receive on the ground.

This data is crucial for global clean energy planning, allowing grid operators and renewables developers to accurately predict how much power their clean energy assets will generate and match it with consumer demand.

Global weather models notoriously struggle to accurately predict precipitation. Rain and snow systems are driven by fast-moving cloud processes on tiny scales that are hard to model accurately using traditional physics-based simulations. Consequently, AI forecasts often produce blurry estimates or miss the boundaries of severe storms entirely.

To solve this, we train our model on two exceptionally high-quality sources of precipitation data: NASA’s satellite-based Integrated Multi-satellite Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) and our own global precipitation reanalysis based on satellite radar.

The result is a significant leap in precipitation forecasting accuracy. In medium-range global forecasts, evaluations against baselines show a Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) improvement of up to 60% against IMERG, 30% for MRMS, and 10% against rain gauge measurements for early lead times.

Figure 3: Medium-range probability of precipitation (PoP > 1mm) forecast comparison. WeatherNext 2 (left) at 25-kilometer resolution shows a highly diffused and pixelated precipitation footprint. WeatherNext 3 (middle) at 11-kilometer resolution closely mirrors the actual satellite ground truth (right), accurately capturing the sharp, convective bands of the weather systems.

Our primary goal is to advance weather intelligence to make it universally useful — whether for an emergency responder tracking sudden wind shifts, an air traffic controller planning flight paths, or a farmer managing crops.

To bring these breakthroughs out of the lab and into the real world, we’re integrating WeatherNext 3 across Google’s core ecosystem and beyond:

The atmosphere will always retain a degree of unpredictability. However, by training on real-world observations and bypassing traditional modeling constraints, WeatherNext 3 brings us closer to a future where forecasts truly match what is happening on the ground.

To learn more about geospatial platforms and AI work at Google, check out Google Earth Engine, AlphaEarth Foundations, and Earth AI.

title: Argentine league to pause games to honour Messi
description: The Argentine football league will pay tribute to Lionel Messi's international career by pausing all their domestic matches in the 10th minute this weekend.
fullText:
The Argentine league will pay tribute to Lionel Messi after his retirement from international football by pausing all of their matches in the 10th minute this weekend for a minute of applause.

The 39-year-old, who wore the number 10 shirt for Argentina, announced his retirement from the national side on Monday.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's final game for his country, who he captained to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, was the 2026 World Cup final defeat by Spain in July.

"In tribute and homage to Lionel Messi's career with the Argentina national team, at the 10th minute of play in all matches the referees will stop the game and a general minute of applause will be held," the Argentine Football Association said.

"We look forward to seeing you on the fields - join us in this recognition!"

Messi, who is Argentina's appearances record holder with 207 caps, first retired from international football in 2016 before reversing his decision.

That followed a defeat by Chile in the Copa America final, in which he missed a penalty in the shootout as Argentina lost a fourth major final in nine years.

The former Barcelona forward went win the World Cup and two Copa America titles with Argentina, scoring a record 125 goals.

Messi made his international debut in 2005 as a 63rd-minute substitute in a 2-1 friendly win over Hungary.

Having moved to Barcelona's La Masia academy as a 13-year-old, Messi has never played senior club football in his native country.

He is the second-highest goalscorer in World Cup history, with 21, behind France's Kylian Mbappe (22), and second for goals in all internationals (125) behind his great rival, Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo (146).

In August, he said he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 following a long illness.

When he announced his retirement from international football, he said following his dad's death he was "even more convinced than before" that he was making the right decision.

He will continue to play in Major League Soccer with Inter Miami, where he has a contract that runs to the end of the 2028 season.

title: 'Dear Katie, how far we have come...' - Taylor gets reply from her hero
description: Ireland's first female world champion writes a letter to Katie Taylor, 30 years after receiving one from her.
fullText:
Before Deirdre Gogarty became Ireland's first female world boxing champion in 1997, she had already inspired a young Irish girl.

A 10-year-old Katie Taylor wrote to her hero in 1996 saying she did not "see boxing for girls taking off here", adding "maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics". As Taylor is set to retire on Saturday as one of Ireland's greatest sportspeople, Gogarty writes back to the 40-year-old...

As I prepare to come home to Ireland to watch you fight at Croke Park, I keep thinking about just how far we have come.

It has been 39 years since I first walked through the doors of a boxing gym in Drogheda and was finally allowed to train.

Back then, I was told women would never be accepted in boxing. That even if we were allowed to compete, nobody would want to watch.

There was a time when I would have given anything simply to be allowed into a ring. We fought in places with few spectators, little recognition, and almost no opportunities for women.

And now, tens of thousands of people will fill one of Ireland's most iconic sporting venues to watch two women box... wow!!!

What was once considered unacceptable has become something an entire nation celebrates.

Katie, what you have done for women's boxing goes far beyond championships, medals, and records.

You didn't simply succeed in the sport - you helped transform how the world sees it, so that another generation of girls never has to question whether they belong.

When I sit among that enormous crowd at Croke Park, I'll be thinking about all the women who fought when nobody was watching.

I'll be thinking about the girls who were told they couldn't and shouldn't.

And most of all, I'll be thinking about the young girls watching you who will never have to ask permission to dream.

With enormous pride and admiration,

Thank you for writing to me and sending me you profile. Sorry I couldn't get back to you sooner as I was doing school exams. I train two nights a week up in my da's club. My da is having his own show in January and he is looking for a fight for me.

I am fed up not being to get fights especially when I see the lads I spar winning championships. There is the European championships for women being held in Sweden in May and my da is trying to enter me into them.

There is an open championship being held in England in April and hopefully I'll be entering that as well. I will let you know how I get on. Sorry to hear your fight in January is looking doubtful (Paddy was telling us).

I hope you can get it on. Hopefully if you get a fight in Ireland, we will all come and see you. My brother Peter recently won the Leinster nine counties and is the reigning champion of the Wicklow/Wexford championship and is fighting in the finals of them again in January on my da's show.

It will be a tough one as his opponent is the All-Ireland champion. I can't see boxing for girls taking off over here in the near future. I can see why you had to go away to get fights.

Hopefully things will change over the next few years but maybe one day they'll even let us box in the Olympics. I hope everything goes well with your boxing career. You have achieved so much already, you have done us all proud. I wish you continued success.

title: Queiroz returns as Ghana manager two months after stepping down
description: Carlos Queiroz is reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team, two months after he appeared to step down following their exit from the World Cup.
fullText:
Carlos Queiroz has been reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team.

The 73-year-old, who had two spells as assistant manager at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson, took charge of the Black Stars in April and led the side to the last 32 at this year's Fifa World Cup, where they were beaten 1-0 by Colombia.

Queiroz appeared to announce his own departure on social media shortly after that defeat, but the Ghana Football Association (GFA) has decided to re-engage him for another spell in charge following internal discussions.

The GFA has not announced the length of his new deal but said he will prepare the team for "a successful new phase on the international stage".

"The GFA believes Queiroz's extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars position him strongly to lead the team into this next chapter," a statement added.

Queiroz has previously led Iran, Portugal and Egypt at major tournaments and has had stints in charge of South Africa, Colombia and Qatar.

Further details on his mandate will be announced by the GFA in due course.

Queiroz will begin his second spell in charge of the West Africans with qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, which begin later this month.

The Black Stars are yet to announce the dates and venues for their first two fixtures in Group C, where they have been drawn alongside Ivory Coast, The Gambia and Somalia.

fullText:
As FromSoftware’s new multiplayer game The Duskbloods nears release, the legendary game director behind Dark Souls talks connection, pessimism and of course, feet

Since 2020’s Demon’s Souls, Japanese video game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has shown the world a different way to think about game design. His games defy convention with punishing fights, obscure rules, and unknowable, inhospitable worlds. The “Soulslike” genre – named after Demon’s Souls and its sequel Dark Souls – is now ubiquitous, influencing multimillion-sellers from God of War and Star Wars: Jedi to Hollow Knight. Miyazaki’s most recent success, 2022’s Elden Ring, which credited Game of Thrones author George RR Martin as a co-creator, sold over 30m copies and inspired Alex Garland to adapt it for the big screen at A24. It earned Miyazaki a spot on Time magazine’s “most influential” list, an accolade he shares with just one other game developer: Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto.

Miyazaki is now 51 and has been FromSoftware’s president since 2014, elevated from game designer to CEO after the success of the Souls series. He has a cherubic face that could pass for 35. He rarely speaks publicly, and never on camera. When he does speak, he answers questions like one of his characters – softly, sadly, his head bowed, making eye-contact only when I am speaking. Outside the studio where we speak is the sprawl of Tokyo’s Shinjuku, an ever-changing maze where tourists get lost and pop-up stores appear and vanish without a trace. Today, a J-pop band performs in the square as the cicadas scream from the trees. A gilded statue of Melania, one of Elden Ring’s toughest bosses, looms over this dimly lit conference room inside From’s headquarters, a bonfire checkpoint away from the chaos.

FromSoftware’s in-game universes are filled with clues – enemies, places and scraps of information from item descriptions paint a vague image of the world, and the player fills the blank space. You never fully understand these domains, although countless YouTube video game theorists have tried – as have other developers in awe of his work. “Of all the many things Miyazaki and his team do well, creating a sense of mystery is the greatest,” explains Dishonored director Harvey Smith, who has more than 40 days’ playtime in Elden Ring. “It’s so incredibly hard to do in video games, which are technical systems … But Miyazaki somehow creates an atmosphere of wonder. Even when finishing, you are left ruminating on fun, murky elements that feel half understood. It’s a delicious sense of intrigue.”

Rather than the single-player action game that Miyazaki’s audience craves (fans are desperate for a sequel to his 2015 gothic masterpiece Bloodborne, for instance), his latest project The Duskbloods is a multiplayer Switch 2 exclusive. Eight players face off against ghoulish horrors, fighting each other to avoid being culled at the end of each round. The survivors are whittled down over three phases culminating in a final three-way battle. The Duskbloods is releasing to an audience with shifting tastes and trends, and it is certainly a risk. “I’m very nervous,” Miyazaki says. “With every title we release there is this mounting tension.”

The game opens with an arresting image: one hand reaching out for another. A male character is slumped on a chair, dejected; the shot moves in close to focus on their draped fingers. From below the frame, a pale hand slowly reaches out and caresses them before gently clasping his wrist. Hands are a recurring motif in Miyazaki’s games; in Elden Ring, massive crawling hands burrow up from underground to attack you, and hand-like giants are revered as deities.

“It’s not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of – maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” Miyazaki says when I ask about this imagery. “Take a look online and there’s a rumour that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from. I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.” (His games have featured, by my count, at least six barefoot female characters.)

Perhaps all the hands and feet are symbolic of human connection. One hand reaches for another; bare feet connect skin with earth. Miyazaki has been exploring that theme since Demon’s Souls, whose novel, stranger-centric multiplayer was inspired by a time his car slipped on an icy hill and a stranger helped to push him to safety. In Demon’s Souls and the Dark Souls series, players paint runes on the ground, which other players can then use to summon help in a fight, creating moments of spontaneous togetherness before an inevitable parting.

While The Duskbloods primarily puts players in opposition, it also explores temporary alliances and conflicting objectives, buoyed by Miyazaki’s love for tabletop role-playing games and board games. Players can even become betrothed to each other, forming an alliance. “I feel it’s less a traditional romance and more a sense of secure trust with a character in the world, and that’s something I personally yearn for,” he says. “It’s not necessarily a romantic pairing – it’s having someone that you can ultimately rely on. This concept is carried through from characters like the maidens in Elden Ring … it’s a transient, ephemeral love, which is maybe a motif I’m striving for.”

The Duskbloods is preoccupied with ruin and rebirth, a thematic cornerstone of From’s games – much as Godzilla was a product of nuclear paranoia in Japan. Even as Miyazaki and I talk, a deadly magnitude 6.8 earthquake hits the Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island, a thousand miles away. If the very ground beneath your feet is unreliable, that can shape your outlook on life, a concept explored extensively in Japanese literature and entertainment, recently on the hit television show Shōgun. “[Ruin and rebirth] is an ongoing theme in a lot of my games, I realise,” Miyazaki says. “That theme on a cosmological scale applies to The Duskbloods as an interesting philosophical area to explore.”

Miyazaki describes himself as a pessimist, a tendency that he believes comes across in his output. That should be obvious to anyone who’s finished any of his games, in which you keep throwing body and blade against seemingly impossible odds, reborn each time you die at a bonfire checkpoint, to try again. Even when you triumph, nothing ultimately seems to change: these games culminate in bleak, morally ambiguous gut-punches, leaving you not as a conquering hero but as the perpetuator of a hopeless cycle. “If we have two ideas of a brighter or dark future, I would tend to sway towards the darker one,” Miyazaki says. “[But] if you explore the ruin and the decay in those worlds, it also lets you explore some chance of rebirth, and I think having that tiny pinprick of light or hope can be something beautiful, something fleeting.”

Sekiro, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, and Elden Ring are all separate series, but they share the same bones. They’re reborn in different forms, to explore fresh ideas, places and perspectives while still playing, feeling and sounding like a FromSoftware game. While it’s immediately clear The Duskbloods is a Miyazaki game, it too wears a different skin, inspired by extraction shooters like Escape from Tarkov and those tabletop role-playing games the director loves. “There’s no intentional FromSoftware [mantra] – ‘this is the way we make our games’ – because if you start to do that it becomes stale and conservative, and you start having to adhere to a set of rules and philosophies, and it just doesn’t become interesting, you can’t make anything that’s as fun,” Miyazaki says.

“So I feel like at least what’s worked for us philosophically is trying to adhere to what we find interesting first. I think that has created a good throughline through our games, and that’s what we concentrate on to [conceive] a new title.”

Back in his early days at the studio, when he was only a coder on the Armored Core series of games, Miyazaki volunteered to take on a struggling project at From – the game that would become Demon’s Souls. (The game was already in trouble, so he felt he had nothing to lose.) He changed everything about the game, and then the game changed everything about his life, as he climbed from coder to company president. From failure was born a game that changed the landscape of video games. Ruin and rebirth.

But does Miyazaki think he has changed? “I don’t intend to,” he says, a smile curling on his lips. “But I probably have.”

title: Norway seizes Russian vessel to enforce $4.22B Ukrainian arbitration claim
description: Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard on Wednesday at the request of Ukraine’s Naftogaz as part of a global effort to enforce a $4.22 billion arbitration ...
fullText:
OSLO, Norway (AP) — Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard on Wednesday at the request of Ukraine's Naftogaz as part of a global effort to enforce a $4.22 billion arbitration award.

Naftogaz is trying to recover the multibillion-dollar arbitration award stemming from Russia's 2014 illegal annexation of Crimea and its seizure of Ukrainian energy assets, including gas fields and pipelines.

In 2023, an arbitration tribunal in The Hague ordered Russia to pay the $4.22 billion to the Ukrainian state-owned energy company for unlawfully seizing its assets in Crimea.

After Russia's refusal to pay the award, Naftogaz has been petitioning national courts seeking court orders to seize Russian commercial assets.

"This is another important step towards restoring justice for Russia's unlawful seizure of Naftogaz assets in Crimea. Russia cannot evade responsibility simply by refusing to comply with an international arbitral award. We will continue to pursue Russian assets around the world," said Naftogaz CEO Sergii Fedorenko.

When asked on Thursday about Norway's action, Russian President Vladimir Putin said the seizure of civilian vessels and strikes on merchant shipping were "acts of state terrorism."

He also condemned recent warnings by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to foreign airlines that flying in Russia would no longer be safe because of Ukrainian long-range drone attacks.

Speaking at the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Russia, Putin linked the vessel seizure and Zelenskyy's warning, saying such incidents "complicated" the prospects for future peace talks. He added that Ukraine's allies were "complicit in international terrorism" by remaining silent on the issues.

Norway's seizure of the Russian vessel, the Professor Molchanov, comes after a Nord-Troms district court order issued August 31, Svalbard Governor Lars Fause said in a statement.

Following the seizure, the vessel is not allowed to leave its current location in Barentsburg on Svalbard, the governor said.

The Russian vessel is used for commercial expedition cruises, including to Svalbard.

title: Sabalenka storms into US Open third round as Pegula, Medvedev advance
description: Aryna Sabalenka took the next step on the road to a rare US Open three-peat, routing qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 to join a raft of contenders cruising into the third round on Wednesday.World number one Sabalenka, without a title since her impressive Indian Wells-Miami double in March was in attack mode as she overpowered 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Iatcenko in just 53 minutes.
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka took the next step on the road to a rare US Open three-peat, routing qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 to join a raft of contenders cruising into the third round on Wednesday.

Men's defending champion Carlos Alcaraz was seeking to join them when he took on Portugal's Jaime Faria in the nightcap on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Alcaraz won his seventh major title at the Australian Open in January but arrived in New York an unknown quantity after a wrist injury forced a four-month layoff that saw him miss Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

He dispelled doubts with a straight-sets first-round victory over Roman Safiullin and will look for further improvement against 72nd-ranked Faria.

World number one Sabalenka, without a title since her impressive Indian Wells-Miami double in March was in attack mode as she overpowered 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Iatcenko in just 53 minutes.

The Belarusian star belted 24 winners, showcasing not only her power from the baseline but also an effective touch at the net.

She dropped just four points on serve in the opening set and was broken just once to give Iatcenko her only game of the second set. Sabalenka responded by winning the next three to secure the win.

"Happy with the level I played today, happy with the focus," said Sabalenka, who will face Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova for place in the round of 16.

Jessica Pegula and former champion Daniil Medvedev also raced into the third round.

World number three Pegula needed just 56 minutes to trounce Sofia Kenin, the former Australian Open champion now ranked 110th, 6-3, 6-1.

Seventh-seeded Medvedev downed US wild card Sebastian Gorzny 6-1, 6-3, 7-5.

Pegula, who is among a trio of players who could supplant Sabalenka atop the world rankings in New York, dropped just seven points on serve.

"I was just trying to stay focused on what I needed to do," said the 2024 US Open runner-up, who next meets another former finalist in Canadian Leylah Fernandez - a 6-4, 6-1 winner over Thailand's Mananchaya Sawangkaew 6-4, 6-1.

Medvedev, who has struggled in the hard court build-up to the year's final Grand Slam, dominated 731st-ranked Gorzny.

He fired 14 aces and saved the lone break point he faced, although he was distracted briefly when a pair of small birds perched on the Louis Armstrong Stadium net and he was forced to replay a point he thought he'd won.

"I saw them straight away and I thought the point would stop straight away and we didn't," Medvedev said. "And the moment I hit the winner we stop. I was not happy with the decision."

Eighth-seeded Ben Shelton prevailed in a tense battle with former world number six Hubert Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6 (7/3), 7-5.

"I thought it was a battle to the end," Shelton said. "I thought Hubi played fantastic today."

American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe was also in action. But another American tipped as a contender -- in-form 16th-seed Brandon Nakashima -- bowed out, upset by 46th-ranked compatriot Alex Michelsen 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

Outside the covered confines of Ashe and the Louis Armstrong Stadium, rain again disrupted play.

Sixth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur finally got his campaign underway in a match postponed from Tuesday but had to wait out another mid-match rain delay on the way to a 6-2, 6-2, 6-4 first-round victory over Italian Andrea Guerrieri.

Lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete of China pulled off a first-round upset, toppling 12th-seeded Spaniard Rafael Jodar 6-2, 6-1, 6-1.

title: Shohei Ohtani injury update adds confusion to perplexing status
description: Shohei Ohtani is expected to have an impact on the postseason as the Los Angeles Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat.
fullText:
Shohei Ohtani is expected to have an impact on the postseason as the Los Angeles Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat.

What opportunities Ohtani might have to make an impact remain uncertain.

Ohtani appeared to be trending in the right direction with his pitching progression, but that was put to a halt on Aug. 29. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced that the team's two-way star would not be making a return as it was anticipated. The pitcher had thrown a 20-pitch bullpen just the day before.

In a Sept. 2 conversation with reporters, Roberts said the team is still considering shutting down Ohtani, but the Dodgers aren't ready to make that decision.

"I know he is in lockstep with (Mark Prior), the pitching guys, the training staff, but I think for me he has to throw a bullpen, then we will see the next progression," Roberts said.

Ohtani is expected to remain available as a designated hitter, but hasn't taken the mound as a pitcher in a game since July 3 due to knee inflammation and biceps discomfort.

Ohtani did not pitch during his first season with the Dodgers, after needing a full year to recover from right elbow surgery.

Roberts was also asked about the possibility of Ohtani playing in the outfield, but the manager declared that's "not on the table."

The Dodgers have not officially shut down Ohtani as a pitcher for the rest of the season. If and when he is cleared and ready to pitch, Ohtani could see limited action on a pitch count before working a full game.

As of Wednesday, Sept. 2, Ohtani was hitting .281 with 88 runs scored, 30 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games this season.

As a pitcher, Ohtani has posted an 8-2 record in 14 starts this season. He's allowed 55 hits, 21 runs (17 earned) and four home runs, while striking out 95.

title: Lawmakers ask Army to explain why it told a military unit to stop specializing in drone warfare
description: A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers is pressing the Army to explain why it told a unit based in Europe to stop specializing in drone warfare, an order that comes as the world's battlefields rapidly e...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers is pressing the Army to explain why it told a unit based in Europe to stop specializing in drone warfare, an order that comes as the world's battlefields rapidly evolve and military tactics increasingly rely on uncrewed systems to fight.

The 173rd Airborne Brigade was building its own drones and practicing the kind of warfare that Ukraine has pioneered against Russia and that Iran has fought against the U.S. — warfare that has killed and wounded American troops. The brigade of 600 soldiers was set up in November to be deployed anywhere that drones were needed.

"We have deep concerns that eliminating this specialized drone unit will limit our ability to learn from allies, particularly the Ukrainian Armed Forces, and hinder our efforts to modernize drone warfare at the speed necessary to compete on the modern battlefield," the lawmakers said in a letter shared with The Associated Press.

It requests a briefing from the Army to explain its decision and was sent Tuesday to departing Army Secretary Dan Driscoll and Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the Army's acting chief of staff. It was signed by Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Republican Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, independent Sen. Angus King of Maine and Republican Rep. Mike Turner of Ohio.

"This specialized unit was a prudent response in a moment when the character of warfare is changing faster than a conventional formation's ability to adapt," the lawmakers say.

They said they were particularly keen to understand the data, analysis and process behind the change after less than a year of the drone unit being active. They also want to know if the decision was based on guidance from Pentagon leadership or made internally by the Army.

LaNeve, who is filling in as the Army's top uniformed officer, recently ordered the battalion to refocus on its core mission of being an airborne infantry unit. The move followed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's sudden ousting of the Army's prior chief of staff, Gen. Randy George.

Integrating drones into the Army's tactics was a major focus for George. Last year, he and Driscoll had rolled out what they called the Army Transformation Initiative, which pushed to add "modernized (unmanned aircraft systems) into formations."

George, who became Army chief of staff under President Joe Biden, regularly spoke about the need to accelerate development of new drone systems and get them in the hands of regular soldiers, not just specialized units. Driscoll supported such efforts and focused on cutting the red tape for military contractors to quickly develop more drones.

After George was ousted by Hegseth without explanation in April, he was replaced by LaNeve. This week, Driscoll submitted his own resignation and later said on social media that Wednesday would be his final full day on the job. A reason for his departure was not publicly revealed, but he was an ally of George, and his tensions with Hegseth have been widely reported.

"We are supportive of the transformative initiatives the Army has taken under Secretary Driscoll's leadership in this area and would like to see that momentum maintained even as uniformed leadership changes," the lawmakers wrote.

Toropin reported from Nuremberg, Germany.

title: International equestrian body lifts ban on Russia
description: The International Equestrian Federation lifts its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.
fullText:
The International Equestrian Federation has lifted its ban on Russian athletes and officials after four and a half years.

Riders, horses and officials from Russia and Belarus have been prohibited from representing their countries under their national flags at FEI events since March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

The international governing body will also allow events to be held in Russia as part of regulations that will come into effect on 5 October.

The move means participants from Russia and Belarus will no longer be required to compete as Neutral Individual Athletes.

The FEI's decision comes after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) announced in June that it would provisionally lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee.

It means athletes from the region could potentially be cleared to represent Russia at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

Following its announcement, the FEI said it would like to "take this opportunity to reiterate its support for the people of Ukraine".

title: Norris sets up junior team to help drivers to F1
description: World champion Lando Norris is setting up his own junior team to support young drivers on their route to Formula 1.
fullText:
World champion Lando Norris says he is putting his own money into setting up a driver development programme and his own team so he can "try to find the next true Formula 1 champion".

Norris' team, to be known as LN4 Fusion, launched on Wednesday on the eve of the Italian Grand Prix weekend. It will run teams across multiple feeder categories starting from next year.

Norris said he wanted to put something back into motorsport after the success he has achieved.

"Why? Because I can," he told BBC Sport in an exclusive interview.

"I have the amazing opportunity to use the bonuses of what was my dream, use the people that I've met, the teams that I've been with and kind of all put it into a big bowl and try and help kind of give back and re-share it with other people and help other people achieve their dream.

"And that's something that almost excites me just as much as saying I wanted to achieve it myself, you know, over the last few years.

"So the fact I can help other people out, that's something I think that's just a beautiful thing in life when you get to do it. And especially if I can do it within the world of motorsport."

Norris said he had "double-ticked" his childhood dreams of getting to Formula 1 and becoming champion, and that this new project "means something and sets a fire inside of me".

He added: "With the Legacy programme first, it's just a perfect opportunity for me to try and give back and support people.

"I know how fortunate I was growing up, having just great opportunities all the time. I know how lucky I was to always be in that position.

"For me, so many things stem from giving. It's what I love to do with my friends, you know, and always take them on holidays and use the bonuses of my job and my life and share it all with them.

"And now I get to do it not only from a personal side with my friends and things, but get to help other drivers, young coming through. To say that and it's even cooler in some ways to help someone else to do that.

"It's a perfect combination. I get to support some drivers I can support. I have timed it so by the time I retire, they are old enough and can take my seat!"

Norris will be in overall charge of the programme but has signed a team of leaders to run it for him while he races full time in F1.

"From a driver development and the legacy programme, I don't think it's something that takes a lot of time.

"It can be a day here or a day there or not even that. It can be a phone call or a text from the drivers that I'm working with saying, can you help me here or do you have any guidance here or whatever it is, you know. So that's not something that takes time.

"That's just a thing that I'm happily willing to do. Everyone knows my focus is still on Formula One. That's my job and that's where all of my focus will be.

"I have a lot of faith and I believe very strongly in the people that we have running the different projects in the day-to-day. And in a way, I feel like I can step back and do nothing and things can still roll on and take place.

"But I want to be a part of it and I want to help in any way I can."

LN4 Fusion will be run by Rene Rosin, founder and former boss of Prema, one of the most successful teams in the junior categories over the past two decades.

In parallel, Norris is setting up what is described as "an independent, fully funded driver development" scheme, to be called the LN4 Legacy Programme.

"I've been really lucky to have some amazing people around me throughout my career, and I know that getting to Formula 1 takes so much more than just talent," Norris said.

"You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time.

"That's what these two projects are all about. LN4 Fusion is about building a race team that can compete with the best in junior motorsport, with great people and a great environment for drivers to develop.

"The LN4 Legacy Programme is about helping talented young drivers get opportunities they might not otherwise have."

Norris' programme will run teams in the Italian F4 Championship, FIA Formula Regional European Championship and FIA Formula 3 Championship in 2027.

The aim is also to compete in Formula 2 next year, but the application process for that has not yet been completed.

Norris will be co-owner of the project along with an investment group run by businessman Dan Richards, who has a background in technology.

The main headquarters of the programme will be in Veneto, Italy.

The UK arm, led by Dan Hazlewood, head of the Fusion Motorsport karting team, will be based in Cambridgeshire and run a programme in British F4.

The young driver programme will be run by Julian Rouse, who was formerly head of a similar programme for the Alpine F1 team.

Richards said: "What we have created is far more than simply the acquisition of a racing team.

"We have assembled a rare combination and secured the right sporting leadership in the industry: an established operation, a Formula 1 world champion, the most successful team principal in junior single-seater racing over the past two decades, world-class motorsport expertise, significant investment and a shared ambition to build a team capable of competing at the highest levels of the sport."

Rosin said: "Having Lando on board adds a further dimension to this project. He has come through the junior single-seater ranks and understands its demands. His involvement will make a real difference to the team."

title: Summer off England duty took me by surprise - Itoje
description: England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially taken aback by the suggestion he step away from international action for the July Tests
fullText:
England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially shocked when head coach Steve Borthwick raised the possibility of him taking the summer off.

Itoje missed England's matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, holidaying in Mauritius and Nigeria as he took a first proper summer break from professional rugby in more than a decade.

The 31-year-old, whose mother died in the weeks before he led England through a deflating Six Nations campaign that featured just one win, says he is now feeling the benefits of his time away.

"I spoke to Steve Borthwick two weeks after the Six Nations and at the end of a long conversation he mentioned we would have to think about what to do in the summer," Itoje told Rugby Union Weekly.

"I was taken aback a bit - it wasn't something that was in my mind.

"At the end of the season it is just the done thing to go on tour.

"But once I had digested it and had thought about it, the more I thought about it, the more I thought it was the best thing for me.

"I'm not annoyed by it at all. It was a wise and prudent decision, it has given me the best opportunity to perform well over the next period of time."

Itoje made his England debut in 2016 and has won 102 caps, as well as touring three times with the British and Irish Lions.

He played more than 30 matches in each of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns, breaching the recommended limit of 2,400 match minutes in the former and narrowly avoiding doing so in the latter.

"I would argue that the mental recovery was far more significant than physically," he said.

"I feel like I'm in a good physical condition, but mentally it was a heavy, busy year, both personally and professionally. So, it was nice to have just a bit of time to take a breath."

Itoje bumped into the England squad at Heathrow Airport as their return from a defeat by the Springboks in Johannesburg coincided with his own from Nigeria.

"I was on the shuttle train back to baggage reclaim and looked to my right and there was [Saracens and England team-mate] Jamie George, I looked to my left and there was Steve Borthwick, and they both looked at me in disbelief," he added.

Apart from that coincidence, Itoje kept his distance from the England set-up over the summer, sending the squad the odd good luck message, but opting against watching their games live.

"It was difficult to do, but when you're supposed to take a break, then if you're living and breathing every moment of a game..." he said.

"I watched them back in retrospect [knowing the final score], partly because I wanted to remove some of the emotion from watching it.

"That's the beauty of live sport - when you watch a game, you're in every nook and cranny, every tackle.

"But that also probably has a hidden emotional weight. The whole purpose of the rest was to get back on the even keel, so that was my methodology."

Itoje's rest precedes another busy period in his life.

Saracens' Prem season begins away to Leicester on 27 September before England take on Australia, Japan, New Zealand and a final's weekend play-off opponent in November's conclusion to the Nations Championship.

And the start of the Rugby World Cup in Australia is a little over a year away.

Meanwhile, his wife Mimi is expecting the couple's first child - a boy - imminently.

"I am very excited," Itoje added

"I want a minimum of three children, I don't really have a maximum.

"My cousin's grandfather must have 60 kids, but that isn't a route I am going down!"

fullText:
As Rockstar’s blockbuster prepares to dominate the headlines, it’s time for the mainstream media to stop treating video games as a novelty that needs explaining

Predictably, the Grand Theft Auto VI “extended look” which premiered on Netflix last week was a success for all involved. The 30-minute preview scorched to No 1 on the viewing chart and even brought the site down for a few minutes as millions of gamers tried to watch what was, effectively, a very long teaser trailer. According to data collated by Eurogamer, more than 9,000 Twitch streamers covered the show leading to 5,227,798 hours of viewing there alone. And this was just the beginning of what will surely be two months of escalating hype – and unprecedented media attention.

Call me cynical, but I suspect the coverage of GTA VI in the media over the next few weeks will follow a familiar pattern. Mostly, it will be five-minute slots wedged in near the end of news bulletins in which games journalists, industry analysts and other pundits will be asked why the game is such a big deal, how much it cost to make and how much revenue it will generate. Perhaps a few will try to reignite the hoary old “violence in video games” debate, there will be presenters laughingly admitting they’ve not touched a game since Pac-Man, rolling their eyes and wallowing in their ignorance, in a way they never would while discussing any other art form. Somebody will venture the subversive view that “games are no longer just for kids”; somebody else will say “games make more money than films and music put together”. And that will be that, job done for another decade … or until there’s a funny story about Pokémon.

I hope I’m wrong. I hope, at least, the BBC, which employs plenty of staff who understand video games, will make time in its schedule to take a good look at GTA VI – its themes and influences, its creators, its place in the wider culture of games and entertainment. Sure, arts coverage on BBC television has been in decline for years, with the broadcaster shifting this content to digital platforms, but I saw plenty of in-depth analysis of Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey, looking at the quality of its translation, its depiction of female characters, its use of practical effects. I didn’t see a single presenter shrugging, looking comedically bewildered and admitting they’d not read Homer since secondary school.

On top of this, whatever mainstream media attention GTA VI does get it will come at the expense of covering other titles. Because, when the next video game story comes up in the wake of Rockstar’s behemoth, TV and radio editors and producers will be thinking, “Oh, we covered games last month.”

The thing is, GTA is a phenomenon – it looks gorgeous, it looks vast, and it will sell many millions of copies. The series’ notoriety transcends the medium. But is it the most interesting video game since GTA V? So much has changed since then. We’ve explored the fascinating, innovative open worlds of Elden Ring, Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and No Man’s Sky (an open galaxy!); we’ve seen brutal adult themes explored in The Last of Us: Part 2 and Silent Hill; we’ve experienced dizzying narrative innovations via Disco Elysium, Split Fiction and Lost Records: Bloom & Rage. All of these deserved at least a portion of that GTA screen and radio time.

True, some games have drawn similar levels of media attention. Minecraft and Fortnite receive regular coverage, but almost always because of concerns over children and games addiction, or because of how they intersect with other media: Minecraft through its hit movie, Fortnite through its many collaborations with music artists. And this is the key problem. Mainstream media is still at the stage where every single games story that does make it to TV or radio has to do the job of explaining and justifying the whole industry. It’s time for programme-makers to understand that video games are a mass cultural phenomenon. Enough people play them and understand them so that they don’t have to be re-introduced every time they’re covered. And most importantly, there is life, love, art and brilliance beyond Grand Theft Auto and beyond the coming storm of hype.

It was my birthday a couple of weeks ago, so I set out to find a simple, fun video game that the whole family could enjoy – and I wanted to share my discovery.

Inspired by Dominik Diamond’s recent column on this very subject, I downloaded the party game What The Dub?!, in which players watch old film clips with portions of the sound dubbed out and then enter their own amusing dialogue to fill the gap. The clips are then re-shown with each player’s text added to the soundtrack via a stilted robotic voice – then everyone votes on the funniest entry. It was hilarious, especially because the clips are from weird old public domain films and TV shows, so everything feels stilted and ridiculous. It’s also simple to take part, with each player using their phone to enter their dialogue choices. Apparently, it’s possible to add new clips via the Steam Workshop, the digital store’s user-generated content feature, but we didn’t figure that out. Regardless, What the Dub?! will definitely be revived at future family celebrations.

Available on: PC

 Estimated playtime: All evening!

EA staff have been speaking anonymously to the industry-news site Game Developer about their concerns after the Saudi-led buyout of Electronic Arts. Some are troubled by the prospect of popular games such as EA Sports FC, Madden and Battlefield being used by Saudi Arabia to distract from its poor human rights record. There are also worries about the company’s culture and job security.

TV producers looking for interesting game stories that don’t involve GTA could check out Eurogamer’s excellent article on the No Man’s Sky’s Galactic Hub project. It’s a community of players exploring and scientifically cataloguing specific regions of the long-running space adventure sim, like a sort of ragtag Starfleet mission. Live long and prosper, lads.

As if making and marketing independent video games isn’t hard enough, several developers have reported thefts at this year’s Gamescom event in Cologne. Posting on X, Mimic creator Ryan Laley said: “Our equipment was stolen last night from the booth. Police reports have been filed. At a loss for words to describe the feeling. Just defeated. Gonna do my best with what’s left of the week. But a huge blow financially and mentally.” According to VGC, others affected included publisher iam8bit and Tessera Studios.

A question from Richard via email:

“My son, aged 6, is a big fan of aeroplanes and is really interested in flight. What games are there that could be used to entertain him, as a thing to do with me. I have (ridiculously) a PS5 and Xbox Series X – is Flight Simulator right? How about Ace Combat? Anything else?”

I’d definitely recommend Microsoft Flight Simulator, which is available on PS5 and Xbox. It can be controlled with just a joypad and you can switch off all the technical elements for your son so he’s basically just steering the craft like in an arcade game. There are lots of aircraft to fly, from tiny prop planes to passenger jets, and you can choose anywhere on Earth to explore. I love simply zooming over cities and scenic highlights, taking it all in.

If you’re ok with him doing a bit of shooting, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is out in October, promising highly detailed visuals and exciting dogfighting. Fans say it looks to be a highlight for the series. I’d also recommend No Man’s Sky, which is a space exploration game, but the flight feels lovely, whether you’re scorching over the surface of a planet or out in the depths of the cosmos. The controls are extremely intuitive too. If he gets into space flight, the slightly more involved Elite Dangerous is worth a look, and for an accessible combination of space flight and shooting, Everspace: Stellar Edition is a really nice option on PS5.
